title: Length is preserved when filtering commutes with mapping
statement: Let $l$ be a finite list with entries in a set $\alpha$, let $f\colon \alpha \to \beta$ be a function, and let $P$ be a decidable predicate on $\beta$. Then applying $f$ to every entry of $l$ and retaining those whose image satisfies $P$ yields a list of the same length as retaining those entries $a$ of $l$ for which $P(f(a))$ holds; that is, the sublist $\bigl(\mathrm{map}\,f\,(l)\bigr)$ filtered by $P$ and the sublist of $l$ filtered by the pulled-back predicate $a \mapsto P(f(a))$ have equal length.
hypotheses_covered: l is a list over a type α
f is a function α → β
P is a decidable predicate on β
replaced:
For a list $l$, a map $f$ and a decidable predicate $P$, the length of the filter of $l.\mathrm{map}\,f$
by $P$ equals the length of the filter of $l$ by the pulled-back predicate $a \mapsto P(f(a))$.
